question.value: What is the physical excitation state of molecular gas in post-starburst galaxies at 0.6 < z < 1.3, and what mechanisms drive their low star formation efficiency?

evidence.quote: By studying the ratio $R_{52} = L'\mathrm{CO(5-4)}/L'\mathrm{CO(2-1)}$, a proxy for the gas excitation, we aim to constrain the physical state of the gas.
The CO excitation helps distinguishing among different mechanisms responsible for the low star formation efficiency (SFE) of post-starburst galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: Non-interacting post-starburst galaxies are undetected in CO(5-4) with stacked R52 < 0.10, indicating cold, diffuse molecular gas and low dense-gas fractions.

evidence.quote: However, when considering only the CO(5-4) non-detections, which also coincide with post-starbusts that do not show signs of interaction, we obtain $R_{52} < 0.10$, twice lower than local star-forming galaxies and more than 2.5 times lower than high-redshift sources.

findings_qualitative.value: Only the three interacting/merging post-starbursts are detected in CO(5-4), showing elevated excitation likely driven by AGN activity, shocks, or merger-driven turbulence rather than star formation.

evidence.quote: Three out of the eight galaxies are detected in CO(5-4). All three show signs of ongoing mergers or interactions
For the merging post-starbursts, however, the higher CO excitation indicates elevated kinetic temperatures, likely induced by shocks and/or AGN activity, which act to suppress star formation.

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular gas and dust appear decoupled in post-starburst galaxies, as none are detected in the dust continuum despite bright CO(5-4) detections in the merging systems.

evidence.quote: Additionally, the fact that our post-starbursts do not agree with the CO(5-4) - L$_\mathrm{IR}$ relation and that none of them is detected in dust continuum indicates that molecular gas and dust in quiescent galaxies might be decoupled, as recently suggested by (cite: Spilker2025).

claims.hypothesis: Low star formation efficiency in non-interacting post-starburst galaxies is driven by a low fraction of dense, warm molecular gas relative to cold, diffuse gas.
claims.experiment: Observed CO(5-4) emission with ALMA in 8 post-SB galaxies at 0.6 < z < 1.3, re-analyzed archival low-J CO data in the uv plane with fixed apertures, and stacked the 5 non-detections.
claims.result: All 5 non-interacting post-SBs are undetected in CO(5-4), yielding a stacked upper limit of R52 < 0.10 (1 sigma), which is 2x lower than local star-forming galaxies and >2.5x lower than high-z sources.
claims.finding: Most post-starbursts are dominated by low-density, low-excitation molecular gas, consistent with quenching maintained by gas stabilization or turbulence preventing collapse.

evidence.quote: However, when considering only the CO(5-4) non-detections, which also coincide with post-starbusts that do not show signs of interaction, we obtain $R_{52} < 0.10$, twice lower than local star-forming galaxies and more than 2.5 times lower than high-redshift sources.

Our results favor a scenario in which most systems are dominated by low-density molecular gas with low excitation, consistent with quenching driven by gas stabilization, feedback regulation, or stripping.

claims.hypothesis: Elevated CO excitation in interacting post-starburst galaxies is driven by non-star-forming heating mechanisms (shocks, turbulence, or AGN) rather than obscured star formation.
claims.experiment: Constructed CO SLEDs up to J=5 for the 3 detected merging post-SBs, compared them with Narayanan et al. (2014) models, and compared L_IR predicted from the Valentino et al. (2020) CO(5-4)-L_IR relation against 3-sigma dust continuum upper limits.
claims.result: Merging post-SBs have mean R52 = 0.40 and SLEDs peaking at J >= 4-5 (with J1448 exceeding models with Sigma_SFR > 500 M_sun yr^-1 kpc^-2), while dust continuum non-detections restrict obscured SFR to < 18 M_sun yr^-1 (20 K) or < 11 M_sun yr^-1 (30 K), far below the 19-142 M_sun yr^-1 implied by CO(5-4).
claims.finding: Residual obscured star formation cannot account for the CO(5-4) emission in merging post-SBs; excitation is instead powered by shocks, turbulence, or AGN activity, and gas and dust are decoupled.

evidence.quote: While undetected galaxies have relatively low SFRs ($\mathrm{SFR \lesssim 20\, M_\odot\, yr^{-1}}$), the three sources with detected CO(5-4) emission would imply significantly higher obscured SFRs ($\mathrm{SFR \sim 20 - 140\, M_\odot\, yr^{-1}}$).

This yielded the maximum $\mathrm{L_{IR}}$ allowed by the lack of continuum detection, and maximum obscured $\mathrm{SFRs < 18\, M_\odot\, yr^{-1}}$, consistent with values expected for quiescent galaxies.
This result reinforces our conclusion from Sec. [4.2](#subsec:sled) that the CO(5-4) emission detected in post-SB galaxies is unlikely to be predominantly powered by ongoing star formation.

why_this_data.value: Selected all publicly available and ALMA-observable z >= 0.6 post-SB galaxies with detected low-J CO lines at the time of proposal to probe denser/warmer gas via CO(5-4).

evidence.quote: They were all the publicly available (to our best knowledge) and observable by ALMA $z \gtrsim 0.6$ post-SBs with detected low-$J$ CO ($J=2,3$) lines at the time when the observations were proposed (cite: Suess2017; Bezanson2021; Zanella2023).
Probing denser and/or warmer molecular gas through CO(5–4) emission provides a key diagnostic of the excitation state of the molecular medium

why_this_method.value: Performed flux measurements in the uv plane with fixed elliptical Gaussian apertures across all channels and transitions to avoid imaging/deconvolution biases, minimize channel noise fluctuations, and ensure identical spatial regions for line ratios.

evidence.quote: Being based on the raw interferometric visibilities, it does not require image reconstruction or deconvolution, avoiding biases and artefacts introduced during imaging and cleaning

We prefer the fixed-aperture approach because it minimizes the impact of noise fluctuations in individual channels, and it ensures that exactly the same spatial region is used when measuring fluxes in different transitions

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Point-source uv model instead of elliptical Gaussian model (tested; yielded CO(5-4) fluxes 1.5x fainter on average, did not affect conclusions)

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, we chose to adopt an extended model rather than a point source, to ensure consistency with the analysis of the low-$J$ CO emission, which in several cases is spatially resolved (Section [3.2](#subsec:co21)).
We verified that using a point-source model yields CO(5–4) integrated fluxes and upper limits that are, on average, 1.5 times fainter.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Circular Gaussian models with channel-varying radii as in Suess et al. (2017) and Bezanson et al. (2021) (rejected in favor of fixed elliptical apertures)

evidence.quote: In contrast, (cite: Suess2017) and (cite: Bezanson2021) adopt circular Gaussian models with radii that vary on a channel-by-channel basis. We prefer the fixed-aperture approach because it minimizes the impact of noise fluctuations in individual channels

how_they_decided_enough.value: Did not refine continuum stacking (e.g., assuming a spectral slope across frequencies) because neither single-band nor multi-band continuum averaging yielded detections.

evidence.quote: Since no detections were found, we did not refine this analysis further, for example by assuming a continuum slope when stacking across different frequency ranges.

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample size (8 galaxies) and few CO(5-4) detections (3 detections) limit statistical correlation analyses.

evidence.quote: We do not find any clear correlation with $D_n4000$Åor $t_\mathrm{q}$, and a mild trend with $f_\mathrm{H2}$ (Fig. [5](#fig:co_ratio_properties)). However, a larger sample with more detections is needed to confirm it.

limitations_admitted.value: Incomplete CO ladder coverage for individual galaxies (e.g., missing CO(2-1) for ID83492 and ID97148; missing intermediate J=3,4 lines for J2258).

evidence.quote: For the remaining merger, only two data points are available (CO(3-2) and CO(5-4)), so additional observations are required to fully constrain the shape of its SLED.

limitations_admitted.value: Sample is biased toward the gas-rich tail of the post-starburst population with pre-existing low-J CO detections.

evidence.quote: We note, however, that our analysis is limited to post-starbursts with existing low-$J$ CO detections, which may represent the gas-rich tail of the population.

limitations_admitted.value: Observations lack the spatial resolution and sensitivity to map spatial variations in excitation, resolve tidal tails in CO(5-4), or perform dynamical stability studies.

evidence.quote: Spatially resolved observations would provide stronger constraints by mapping the extent of both high-$J$ and low-$J$ CO emission and identifying potential spatial variations in excitation across the galaxies.

referee_caveats_inferred: Inconsistent conversion ratio R32 assumed across sections: Section 4.1 and Table 3 use R32 = 0.62 to estimate pseudo-CO(2-1) for ID83492 and ID97148, whereas Section 4.2 states R32 = 0.50 was used for the SLED normalization.
Inconsistent reporting of the mean R52 for merging post-starbursts: Abstract, Section 4.1, and Table 4 state R52 = 0.40, while Section 6 (Summary and conclusions) states R52 ~ 0.49.

Using an extended elliptical Gaussian model on unresolved CO(5-4) data inflates fluxes and upper limits by a factor of ~1.5 compared to a point-source model, which could bias R52 upward if the CO(5-4) emission is more compact than the low-J CO aperture.
